name: Foodberry
old_description: Foodberry is an innovation company that partners with leading brands to create better bite-sized snacks that are delicious, wholesome, and convenient.
about:
Foodberry is based in Boston, Massachusetts. The company was founded by David Edwards, a longtime Harvard professor and founder of AIR and Sensory Cloud, with its proprietary food‑tech platform initially developed in labs at Harvard and MIT before moving into a first‑of‑its‑kind manufacturing facility.

Foodberry creates bite‑sized snacks using a plant‑based coating technology that turns virtually any food or beverage into a self‑contained, no‑mess product. The company operates a 42,000‑square‑foot, GFSI/SQF Level 2‑certified production facility in Boston and offers three core services: product development with an in‑house R&D team, co‑manufacturing for brand partners, and technology transfer to integrate its coating process into existing production lines.

Its customers are food and beverage brands seeking growth‑driving snack innovations. Publicly named partners include the Bel Group (parent of Laughing Cow and GoGo SqueeZ), Van Leeuwen Ice Cream, Gopuff, and Cape Cod Select, with collaborations spanning fruit‑based snacks, ice‑cream bonbons, and frozen smoothie bites.

The venture was started to tackle two systemic problems: making convenient, craveable foods without sacrificing nutrition, and reducing plastic packaging across the food system. Foodberry’s stated aim is to make the future of snacking as nutritious, delicious, and planet‑friendly as a natural berry.

name: Forj Medical
old_description: We’re your all-in, hands-on 100% medical focused CDMO partner, whether you need high-volume global manufacturing or custom full system development.
about:
Forj Medical is headquartered in Arden Hills, Minnesota, with additional facilities in St. Paul and Vadnais Heights. The company operates as a global contract design and manufacturing organization (CDMO) focused exclusively on medical devices. While its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the firm emphasizes decades of technological and clinical experience across high-stakes medical applications.

The CDMO provides end-to-end services from design and development through high-volume production. Its vertically integrated capabilities include precision molding, PCBA manufacturing, automation, cable assembly, cleanroom operations, polymer and metal 3D printing, and supply chain management. Forj Medical reports assembling more than 250 million devices and components annually across 450,000 square feet of manufacturing space spread over six global sites in the United States, Costa Rica, Singapore, and Indonesia. The company supports programs ranging from 10 units to 10 million units per project.

Forj Medical serves medical device OEMs across application areas such as fluid and gas management, surgical energy, optical systems, electromagnetic navigation systems and sensors, stimulation and active wearables, and consumables and components. Named customers include Conavi Medical, a Fortune 500 medical device manufacturer, and Vocxi Health, which partnered with Forj to miniaturize a breath-based cancer detection platform.

The company positions itself as a single-source partner that becomes an extension of its clients' teams, offering integrated quality management (ISO 13485 certified with five FDA establishment registrations) and a digital portal for continuous project visibility. Clients cite Forj's willingness to redesign systems from the ground up and maintain collaboration under one roof as they scale toward regulatory clearance.

old_description: I have been running production for our company since 2022. Even in just these few years, I cannot recall how many times FormTight has come through for us. They have been accommodating, flexible, and understanding with each order and revision we have placed with them. They have also gone above and beyond in committing resources to our product, being willing to spend additional time with our R & D team to assure and improve quality. Their service and quality have given me the peace of mind that I am confident we would not receive elsewhere. Vendors like FormTight are hard to come by. They have been a valuable partner in our success, and I am confident that will continue to be the case moving forward.
about:
FormTight, Inc. was founded in 1992 and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado. The custom plastic thermoforming company has operated for over three decades, specializing in both thin- and thick-gauge thermoforming for food, medical, industrial, and retail markets.

The company handles every stage of the packaging lifecycle in-house at its Denver facility, from consultation and design through prototyping, mold manufacturing, and full production. Capabilities include thin-gauge thermoforming for food and medical packaging, thick-gauge thermoforming for durable components, 5-axis CNC routing for complex geometries, and an in-house scrap grinding operation that recycles material back into the supply chain. Materials processed range from PET, PVC, ABS, HIPS, HDPE, PP, PETG, to polycarbonate.

FormTight serves manufacturers across food packaging, medical packaging, industrial thermoforming, and retail packaging. Long-term customers include Innovative Brick Systems and Dazzling Displays in Denver, Taylor Tools in Denver, Camerons Products in Colorado Springs, and Arm Automation in Austin, Texas. Testimonials highlight the firm's ability to reengineer packaging for cost reduction, expedite aggressive schedules, and provide tooling expertise such as selecting male versus female tool designs.

FormTight emphasizes attention to detail, competitive pricing, on-time delivery, and high-quality finished products. The company states that keeping all processes under one roof gives it control over quality and lead times, while its sustainability focus closes the loop on waste through internal recycling. The team's hands-on thermoforming experience and willingness to tackle challenging designs have retained customers for over three decades.

name: Forum Plastics LLC
old_description: Forum offers a full suite of assembly services in an ISO Class 7 cleanroom, producing 100,000-200,000 parts per month.
about:
Forum Plastics LLC operates from Watertown, Connecticut. The company traces its roots to 1992 when GM Tool & Forum Molding Inc. was founded. In 2009, ownership was consolidated under Forum Plastics Inc., and in 2016 the business was acquired by Squadron Capital, a private equity group that reinvests proceeds into technology enhancements. The leadership team includes President Mark Polinsky and Vice President Andrew Butkus.

The company provides injection molding services with a focus on complex geometries, insert molding, over molding, and micro molding for parts as small as 0.005 cubic inches. It operates an ISO Class 7 cleanroom for assembly and packaging, and offers in-house mold design, fabrication, and repair through a full-service tool room equipped with CNC machining centers, EDM machines, and precision grinding. Additional capabilities include pad printing, laser marking, rapid prototyping, and advanced metrology such as industrial CT scanning, CMM, and VMM inspection. Monthly production volumes range from 100,000 to 200,000 parts, supported by a staff of 101 employees across a facility that added 10,000 square feet in 2015 and moved to a new location in December 2025.

Forum serves the medical device, life sciences, industrial, and military/defense markets. Its customer base spans early-stage startups to global original equipment manufacturers, with the company emphasizing support through concept planning, design for manufacturability, regulatory process navigation, and full-scale commercialization.

Forum differentiates itself as an engineering-based contract manufacturer that reinvests in new equipment—such as Arburg micro molders, Keyence measurement systems, and additive freeform 3D printing—to accelerate project timelines. The company highlights its ability to move from prototype to production in days rather than months, and its ITAR registration enables work on defense-related programs.

old_description: Four Engines Apparel | Embroidery & Printing – Personalization & brand gear in Massachusetts
about:
Four Engines Apparel operates from a dedicated shop at 201B West Boylston Street in West Boylston, Massachusetts. The company was established in 2020 by Dave Keddy, who began the venture as a home-based business in his basement before growing a customer base that supported a move into a standalone facility. Keddy brought over 17 years of prior experience in logo merchandising and apparel decoration to the operation.

The shop provides embroidery, screen printing, custom patches, and heat transfers on a range of apparel and fabric types. Work is performed in-house, allowing direct control over each decoration process. The owner emphasizes personal communication and attention to detail across every order, from single items to larger runs, without publishing specific facility dimensions or headcount figures.

Customers include local small businesses, musical acts, sports teams such as youth soccer programs, and specialty organizations like Expedition Reptile, which uses embroidered show shirts for weekly performances. The business explicitly positions itself to serve low-quantity orders that larger contract decorators often decline, targeting community groups, startups, and independent brands needing branded gear in smaller volumes.

Keddy cites a dual motivation: a passion for the rhythm of production processes — likened to his background as a musician — and a long-term goal to create or partner with a charity that funds community music programs. The name "Four Engines" originates from a drumming term that has resonated with him since a lesson years ago.

Four Fields Furniture operates from West St. Paul, Minnesota, in the Twin Cities metro area. Founded in 2014 by Adam Bischoff, the family-owned shop began as a one-person woodworking studio focused on heirloom-quality custom furniture. Bischoff, a craftsman, started building pieces by hand for local clients, emphasizing solid hardwoods and steel accents.

The shop produces made-to-order hardwood furniture, specializing in dining tables (including live-edge slab designs), coffee tables, side tables, desks, entryway benches, sideboards, bookshelves, and wood-and-steel combinations. It also builds custom religious items such as kneelers, altars, and credence tables, and offers professional table refinishing. All work is performed in the company's Minnesota woodshop; no facility size or headcount figures are disclosed, but output is characterized as one piece at a time.

Four Fields serves residential customers throughout the Twin Cities, including Minneapolis, St. Paul, and surrounding suburbs. Its clientele consists primarily of homeowners seeking custom pieces for their homes, with the company noting trust from "Twin Cities families" and over 100 five-star Google reviews. Delivery and setup are provided across the metro area.

The company distinguishes itself through handcrafted construction, attention to detail, and a design process that tailors each piece to the client's space and style. Bischoff cites honest communication, the use of premium domestic hardwoods (walnut, oak, cherry, maple, ash, mahogany, parota) and in-house steel bases, and a 50% deposit/50% completion payment structure as part of its approach. The shop also extends the life of existing furniture through refinishing services.

The company repairs, maintains, rebuilds, installs, and sells commercial cooking, food processing, and refrigeration equipment from most major brands. Its service portfolio covers walk-in coolers and freezers, refrigerated display cases, ice machines, gas and electric ovens, fryers, grills, charbroilers, steam cookers, mixers, dough rollers, slicers, meat processing equipment, and dishwashers. Franklin Food Equipment also maintains a large inventory of OEM parts and offers rebuilt equipment as an alternative to new purchases, alongside preventative maintenance plans designed to catch wear before it causes downtime.

The customer base includes restaurants, commercial bakeries, food preparation operations, grocery stores, meat processors, schools, medical and nursing facilities, and correctional facilities — essentially any operation with a commercial kitchen. Technicians are dispatched on-site across the service area, which includes cities such as Fort Smith, Russellville, Conway, and Mena in Arkansas, and Talihina, Wilburton, Stigler, and Poteau in Oklahoma.

The company emphasizes its factory-trained technicians, extensive parts inventory, and rapid on-site response as the foundation of its value proposition. By combining sales, installation, repair, and preventative maintenance under one roof, Franklin Food Equipment aims to serve as a single point of contact for commercial kitchen operators looking to minimize equipment downtime.

Freudenberg Medical is headquartered in Minnetonka, Minnesota, and operates as part of the Freudenberg Group, a family-owned enterprise with more than 175 years of experience developing high-performance materials. The company provides vertically integrated services across 12 manufacturing sites and two sales offices worldwide, encompassing 813,000 square feet of production space and a workforce of over 2,700. Core capabilities include silicone molding and extrusion, thermoplastic injection molding and extrusion, precision metal tubing and hypotube fabrication, specialty needle manufacturing, hydrophilic and drug-eluting coatings, and complex catheter design and assembly. Freudenberg Medical serves medical device and biopharma customers globally, with recent expansions adding catheter manufacturing capacity in Jeffersonville, Indiana, and Galway, Ireland, as well as high-volume thermoplastic extrusion in Coyol, Costa Rica. The company's CleanAssure ISO Class 5 cleanroom provides controlled cleaning and sterilization for sterile single-use assemblies, while its LUBRITEQ hydrophilic coating platform addresses friction reduction and trackability for interventional devices.

The business emphasizes end-to-end partnership, combining clinical insight with deep materials expertise in silicones, thermoplastics, metals, and coatings to de-risk complex projects. Acquisitions such as Fuji Seiko (Japan), APEC (California and China), MedVenture (Indiana), and Jenline Industries (Massachusetts) have broadened its technology portfolio and geographic reach.

The founders frame the mission as empowering entrepreneurs to achieve goals whether they seek a family-sustaining business or a nationwide brand.

Barcus emphasizes a client-first approach, offering no-cost design consultations, requiring no more than a 30% deposit, and providing shop drawings or samples for approval before fabrication begins. By eliminating subcontractor markups and optimizing each design for the client’s specific load profile, the company aims to deliver the lowest lifetime energy cost.

Engineering was positioned as a core differentiator early on, with the team creating custom tools and processes for each job. Today GLW highlights value engineering, design flexibility, and fixtures engineered for easy installation as key advantages, aiming to deliver a hassle‑free experience from napkin sketch to final install.

about:
GOEX Apparel operates from Kansas City, Missouri, where it manages printing, warehousing, and distribution for a supply chain that spans the Western Hemisphere. The company is structured as a certified B-Corp and verified member of the Fair Trade Federation, Social Enterprise Alliance, and Fair Labor Association, though its founding year and original founders are not publicly disclosed.

The company produces custom-printed apparel and wholesale blank basics, including eco-triblend tees. Fabrics are knitted in South Carolina from U.S.-sourced materials, then cut and sewn at GOEX's owned factory in Haiti. Finished garments are printed and shipped from the Kansas City facility, creating a 2,700-mile supply chain—far shorter than the industry average of six global circumnavigations.

GOEX serves organizations needing branded merchandise, retail-ready wholesale basics, and tour merchandise for musicians. Its customer base includes the Minnesota Historical Society, Black Hills Basecamp, Biomes Marine Biology Center, and Koraa, all cited as verified buyers.

The business was built to create fair-wage jobs in Haiti, paying 65 percent above the local apparel-sector minimum so that each employee can support an average of six family members. It also prioritizes OEKO-TEX ECO PASSPORT certified fabrics and Fair Trade certified labels, positioning every order as a driver of family stability and reduced environmental impact.

Gartland Distributors began in 1999 when Bob Gartland started selling beef jerky from his pickup truck in Biddeford, Maine. With support from his wife Kate, their family, and longtime partner Ron Soucy, the one-man operation grew into a snack distribution business serving central and southern Maine. In June 2025, ownership passed to Jim and Christine Faiella, experienced small-business owners who have run community markets in the region for over 15 years.

The company distributes a full line of snack foods including nuts, trail mixes, candy, meat snacks, and healthier alternatives, plus vending products. Its service model includes product rotation, merchandising, and inventory ordering for customers, with delivery coverage stretching from central Maine to the southern coast. Operating from a facility in Arundel, the distributor maintains a broad inventory and provides full-service support including vending machine stocking. The product catalog also highlights items made in Maine.

Gartland’s customer base spans hospitals, schools, health centers, markets, and local shops and businesses throughout its service area.

The company emphasizes personal service and local relationships, a 100% guarantee program, competitive pricing, and a focus on Maine-made products as its key differentiators.

name: Gary Weeks and Company Furnituremakers
old_description: We design and build furniture to the highest standards of craftsmanship, ergonomics, beauty, and longevity. We ship worldwide.
about:
Gary Weeks and Company Furnituremakers was founded in 1992 in Wimberley, Texas, a small Hill Country town. The company operates as a custom woodworking shop, though its ownership structure is not publicly disclosed. From the start, the focus has been on designing and building furniture that meets high standards of craftsmanship, ergonomics, beauty, and longevity.

The shop produces a range of solid-wood furniture, with the Weeks Rocker® as its signature piece. The product line includes rocking chairs in cherry, walnut, maple, and mesquite; dining chairs (Wilson, Williams, Webb models); dining tables (trestle, pedestal, leg-and-apron styles); barstools; and custom pieces such as desks, cabinets, and tables. Production relies on traditional mortise-and-tenon joinery, hand sculpting and sanding, and hand-rubbed oil or varnish finishes. The facility houses a woodshop, showroom, finishing rooms, and a lumber shed, supported by custom machines, jigs, compressed air, and dust collection. The company describes itself as a small, custom shop that ships worldwide.

The company sells directly to individual customers across the United States and internationally, including Europe, Australia, Asia, Africa, and South America. Its website references more than 1,500 patron reviews, indicating a consumer-focused clientele rather than industrial or contract buyers. No specific industry verticals are cited beyond residential furniture and custom woodworking.

The company emphasizes several differentiators: a comfort guarantee on its rocker that includes a full refund with round-trip shipping paid by the shop; a commitment to “no cookies, no popups, no ads” on its website; and a depth of online detail covering design criteria, wood selection, and construction methods. The founders’ intent, as reflected in a quoted Barbara Tuchman passage, is that quality requires intensive effort and honesty of purpose.

about:
Gentuity, LLC is based in Sudbury, Massachusetts. The company was founded by alumni of the original LightLab team, the group that pioneered the first-generation optical coherence tomography (OCT) systems deployed in catheterization laboratories worldwide. Drawing on decades of experience in intravascular imaging, the founders set out to overcome the limitations of traditional OCT technology.

The company develops and manufactures the HF-OCT Imaging System paired with the 1.8F Vis-Rx PRIME Micro-Imaging Catheter. The high-frequency OCT platform captures rapid, full-length coronary imaging in a single one-second pullback, delivering high-resolution views of vessel anatomy. The system is designed for plug-and-play integration into existing cath lab workflows without requiring sterile bags.

Gentuity serves interventional cardiologists and hospital catheterization labs focused on complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) procedures. Clinical case studies feature physicians from Tampa General Hospital and The Christ Hospital. In the United States, the company's advanced intravascular imaging solutions are distributed through a partnership with GE HealthCare.

The venture was launched to address the shortcomings of conventional OCT systems, aiming to provide complete vessel visualization and real-time insights that enable confident treatment planning. By combining expertise in optics, software, and interventional cardiology, Gentuity seeks to simplify complex procedures and advance cardiovascular innovation in line with international guidelines.

about:
George C. Moore operates from Westerly, Rhode Island, where the company was founded in 1909 as the George C. Moore Company. The business remains a privately held, family-owned enterprise and serves as the parent of two wholly owned divisions: George C. Moore Company, which produces stretch and rigid narrow fabrics in woven and knit constructions, and Darlington Fabrics, which manufactures stretch and rigid wide warp knit fabrics.

The company manufactures narrow elastic fabrics and rigid webbings for a range of end uses. Its U.S. headquarters in Westerly houses sales, engineering, design, research and development, and technical support, while a vertical weaving and knitting facility established in 2006 in American Park Free Zone, El Salvador, handles production from ¼-inch to 12-inch widths. That site also provides in-house dyeing and finishing, rotary printing, cutting and sewing, performance finishes, and customized packaging.

Customers span swim, dance, and yoga apparel; underwear waistbands and trims; ballistic protection for military and law enforcement; flame-resistant work uniforms; safety and industrial webbing; team sports gear such as goggles and pads; performance compression and activewear; and orthopedic and medical products including latex-free, hook-receptive, and plush-surface elastics.

The founding premise of “providing continual innovation and support to our valued customers” has guided the company for over 110 years. It emphasizes competitive pricing, consistent quality, and on-time delivery, backed by two R&D divisions and sustainability programs that have cut heating and cooling energy by 35%, lighting energy by 40%, water usage by 44%, and achieved recycling rates of 33% for wooden pallets, 15% for corrugated boxes, and 100% for plastic process bags.

The primary customers are outdoor enthusiasts—duck hunters, sport anglers, and commercial fishermen—who operate in extreme shallow-water environments such as cypress swamps, mud trenches, and rock-laden rivers. Go-Devil emphasizes that its products are designed and tested in the harshest conditions the company can find, and that its in-house manufacturing and comprehensive parts stock enable customer service that it describes as second to none. Wayne’s direct involvement ensures that no pine or construction‑grade lumber enters the shop, and the finish process includes up to three stain samples cut from the project’s own off‑cuts so clients can verify color in their own lighting. The company positions itself on quality over quantity, emphasizing materials and craftsmanship that exceed mass‑produced imports.

about:
Great Divide Fabrication LLC, operating as Great Divide Services, is based in Buffalo, Wyoming. The company was launched in 2018 by Erik Burden, a master mechanical technician who began his career as an apprentice and advanced to journeyman and manager before starting the business. Burden owns the company with his wife Jenn, and they run it with a small team.

The company provides heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and gas piping services for residential and commercial customers. Its offerings include installation of furnaces, heat pumps, infrared garage heaters, split systems, ductless mini-splits, and rooftop units. It also performs custom sheet metal fabrication and decorative tin work, and sells metal, piping, and related supplies. The shop operates with 24-hour emergency service availability.

Great Divide serves homeowners and businesses in Buffalo and surrounding Wyoming communities. Its residential clients rely on the company for furnace and air-conditioning installation, annual maintenance, and emergency repairs. Commercial customers include those needing package units and rooftop systems. The company also supports custom fabrication projects for both residential and light commercial applications.

Burden founded the business to deliver outstanding customer care and high-quality craftsmanship, emphasizing a collaborative work environment and continuous improvement. The company highlights its 24-hour service and the owner’s hands-on technical expertise as key differentiators.

name: Great Plains Energy Corridor
old_description: The Corridor was tasked with providing innovative approaches that bring people together to advance the development of North Dakota's abundant and diverse energy resources.
about:
The Great Plains Energy Corridor operates from Bismarck, North Dakota, where it was established in 2008 as a division of Bismarck State College. The initiative was launched through the efforts of former U.S. Senator Byron Dorgan with a mandate to develop innovative approaches that connect stakeholders and advance the state's diverse energy resources.

The Corridor does not manufacture physical products. Instead, it provides information, education, outreach programs, and special events on topics ranging from enhanced geothermal systems and renewable fuels to sustainable development and energy transmission and storage technologies. It leverages Bismarck State College's nationally recognized energy education programs, which deliver state-of-the-art training to current and future industry employees. The office is housed in the National Energy Center of Excellence (NECE) building on the college campus, a facility dedicated in September 2008 that incorporates a ground-source geothermal heat pump system, LEED-specification lighting, a total energy heat recovery system, and Flexcrete — a construction material made with fly ash from coal combustion.

The organization serves partners across government, education, and the private sector, helping to secure federal funds and other resources for energy-related projects that benefit North Dakota. Its audience includes energy industry employers, policy makers, educators, and students pursuing energy technology careers. The Corridor also produces an annual report highlighting North Dakota energy industry statistics and hosts the EmPowerND Energy Conference, though the Fall 2023 edition was canceled.

The Corridor was created specifically to foster collaboration that accelerates energy development in North Dakota, positioning the state as a vibrant and innovative energy hub. Its differentiation lies in its direct integration with a college energy curriculum, its physical presence in a high-efficiency demonstration building, and its role as a conduit for federal energy funding into regional projects.

Green Bay Plastics, Inc. was incorporated in 1957 in Green Bay, Wisconsin, initially as part of Mosinee Paper Corporation. In 1989, J. Kevin Hogan and his wife JoAnn led a buy-out, returning the company to family ownership. Today it remains family-owned and operated, with Michael Hogan as president and general manager, Patrick Hogan as vice president, and Kathleen Hogan-Lesatz as controller and secretary-treasurer.

The company specializes in custom blow molding, producing plastic bottles, jars, canisters, containers, and wheels. They design and build their own manufacturing machinery, auxiliary equipment, and tooling in-house. Production runs range from a few thousand units to mass-production volumes. Additional services include labeling, painting, and special packaging.

Green Bay Plastics serves a range of industries including food and beverage, lubricants, personal care, dietary supplements, medical and healthcare, household products, sporting goods, toy components, and general industrial applications. Customers include wholesale distributors and brand owners seeking custom packaging and components.

The company emphasizes self-sufficiency through proprietary equipment design and in-house tooling, which it says allows tighter control over lead times and part complexity. The family ownership structure is cited as a driver of long-term customer relationships and consistent quality.

about:
Green Brook Electronics was founded in 1974 in Green Brook, New Jersey, and has operated as a supplier of electronic components and instrumentation for five decades. In 2018, the company relocated to a facility in North Plainfield, New Jersey, that is more than seven times larger than its original store, expanding its capacity for inventory and services.

The business stocks over 300,000 distinct line items across multiple warehouse locations, ranging from semiconductors, relays, capacitors, and resistors to wire, cable, fuses, and audio/video cables. Beyond distribution, Green Brook Electronics operates a retail store open to the public, a rental center for test equipment, a repair center capable of board-level and surface-mount work on items such as medical devices and tube amplifiers, a movie prop center offering vintage test equipment and computers for film productions, a technology studio providing soldering and Arduino lessons, a vinyl record shop, and a component identification service called Component Eye-D.

Customers include large technology firms, industrial buyers, hobbyists, film production companies, and students seeking hands-on electronics training. The company ships worldwide and emphasizes its ability to source obsolete or long-lead-time parts.

Green Brook Electronics positions itself as a solution provider rather than a simple distributor, highlighting its repair expertise, obsolete-part sourcing, and the breadth of services — from rentals to education — under one roof.

Green Mountain Furniture has operated in Ossipee, New Hampshire, since 1975. Named for the mountain range that borders the property, the business began as a destination for home furnishings in the Lakes Region and has grown into a 40,000-square-foot showroom spanning multiple floors.

The company functions as a full-line furniture retailer rather than a manufacturer. Its showroom stocks living-room, bedroom, dining, home-office, and cabin-style collections from brands such as Craftmaster, Flexsteel, and Best Home, along with mattresses (innerspring, memory foam, and latex), adjustable bases, area rugs, lighting, and decorative accessories. A delivery team also provides removal of existing pieces at the time of drop-off.

The primary customer base is residential shoppers furnishing primary and vacation homes, though the product mix includes medical-grade vinyl lift recliners that serve accessibility and healthcare needs. Shoppers can browse dozens of recliners, sofas, and beds without pressure from commission-based staff.

The founder's original pitch — “more than meets the eye” — still frames the value proposition: a large, low-pressure showroom where customers can physically test products, backed by a 100-night sleep trial on mattresses and a five-year Guardsman stain warranty on upholstery.

old_description: Moser has been leading the competition since 1986 and continues to provide industry leading products. We pride ourselves in our ability to supply quality America-made products, at an affordable price
about:
Moser Engineering operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in Portland, Indiana. The company was founded in 1986 by Greg Moser, who initially launched the business to support his own drag-racing habit at the Muncie strip. Today it remains family owned and operated.

The shop produces custom axles, complete rear-end assemblies, housing service parts, differential options, brake packages, and chassis/suspension components. All manufacturing — forging, heat treating, and machining — is done in-house using steel sourced exclusively from U.S. mills. The facility handles GM, Ford, and Mopar applications for drag, circle-track, street-rod, and off-road vehicles.

Customers range from weekend racers and project-car builders to professional teams running circle-track and drag cars. Moser supplies custom axle sets for Jeeps and trucks, full-floater rears for oval competition, and turnkey Muscle Pak rear assemblies for high-end builds. The company also offers parts, fluids, and service items through its online catalog.

Moser cites three pillars for its reputation: domestic manufacturing with full process control, a two-business-day turnaround on most custom orders, and validation via an in-house race team that campaigns two rigs and multiple cars. Staff members, many of them longtime racers and builders, test components on the track before they reach the market.

name: Grillo & Co
old_description: Grillo and Co creates beautiful bespoke furniture for your home or workplace. Operating almost entirely by commission, we custom design and hand make each piece to your exact specifications at our workshop in Golden, Colorado. We will help you visualize your ideas and, once you’re completely happy with the proposed design, we hand-craft your unique heirloom piece of furniture.
about:
Grillo & Co operates a woodworking workshop in Golden, Colorado, where founder John Grillo creates bespoke furniture on commission. Grillo trained at the Thomas Chippendale International School of Furniture near Edinburgh, Scotland, where his work earned the Richard Demarco Prize and recognition in Furniture & Cabinetmaking Magazine. He is a member of the Fine Furniture Guild and established his practice in Golden after completing his studies.

The company custom designs and hand-builds each piece, using processes that include 3D design visualization, dovetail joinery, parquetry, tambour door construction, and veneering. Projects range from dining tables and writing desks to console tables and record cabinets, all crafted from solid woods such as walnut, maple, cherry, and exotic veneers. The workshop handles every stage from concept to finish, though no facility size or headcount figures are published.

Grillo & Co serves residential and commercial clients seeking one-of-a-kind furniture for homes and workplaces. Past commissions include a walnut coffee table built to exact dimensions, a federal-style writing desk with birds-eye maple accents, a radial dining table with interlocking legs, and a tambour-door record cabinet. Customers work directly with Grillo through home or office visits and receive progress updates throughout the build.

The firm distinguishes itself through Grillo's award-winning craftsmanship, his training at a world-furniture school, and membership in the Fine Furniture Guild. The bespoke model eliminates supply-chain constraints common among commercial retailers, and clients buy directly from the designer, allowing involvement down to the style of dovetails and choice of materials.

Groves Bros. serves customers in the interior design and furnishing sectors, specifically those specifying fabrics for drapery, upholstery, and wall covering projects. Its clientele includes designers, workrooms, and specifiers seeking custom, artisanal textiles for residential and commercial spaces.

The firm's stated distinction lies in its commitment to handcrafting every fabric, ensuring no two pieces are identical, and in drawing on Venetian textile heritage to create what it calls timeless fabrics. The company has completed projects such as the New Severn Run High School auditorium and stadium, and the Church of the Resurrection.

HP Electronics serves education, healthcare, corporate and commercial, hospitality, government and public sector, entertainment and performance venues, houses of worship, and retail clients. Notable installations include projects for New Severn Run High School and the Church of the Resurrection, demonstrating expertise in educational and worship environments.

Early international work included designing and installing one of the first modern sound systems in mainland China, and the firm aims to be the most sought-after electronic systems contractor in the industry.

old_description: Engineering teams, project managers, and procurement buyers trust H&H to take a tight spec and fabricate it into something that ships when we say it will. St. Louis-based, serving customers across the region and beyond since 1947.
about:
H&H Metal Fabrication has operated from St. Louis, Missouri since 1947, when the Finazzo family began manufacturing light fixtures in the same building that housed the H&H radio shop. The company remained under continuous family ownership for more than seven decades before transitioning in 2019 to women-owned leadership under Carolyn Farrell (President) and Morgan Jarrett (COO), with Kevin Farrell serving as CFO.

The shop specializes in custom metal fabrication built to print, including electrical enclosures, e-houses, and enclosure modification services such as cut-outs, drilling, and threading. A 500-ton, 22-foot press brake anchors the forming capacity at their downtown plant on South 22nd Street, and full in-house painting capabilities support finish requirements. The team handles one-off prototypes as well as repeat production runs for larger assemblies.

Customers range from engineering firms and procurement buyers to electrical contractors and manufacturers. Notable projects include fabricating the attachment mechanism for the Chihuly Blue Chandelier reinstallation at the Missouri Botanical Garden, supplying light housings for the new exterior lighting at St. Louis City Hall, and supporting lighting projects for Villa Lighting Supply across the U.S. and Canada.

The company emphasizes quality craftsmanship and first-class customer service as its founding standards, maintained through the ownership transition. WBENC certification as a Women's Business Enterprise provides a procurement advantage for clients with supplier-diversity requirements.

Hawaii Technology Development Corporation (HTDC) is a state economic development agency headquartered in Honolulu, Hawaii. HTDC operates the state's Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) center, known as INNOVATE Hawaii, which provides business development services and manufacturing assistance to small and medium-sized manufacturers across all islands. The agency also runs the Hawaii Center for Advanced Transportation Technologies (HCATT), with over 20 years of hydrogen and fuel cell research in partnership with the U.S. Air Force. HTDC offers co-working space, educational programs, funding access, mentoring, and workforce development through initiatives like the Holiday Tech Job Fair. The agency reports securing $62 million in federal funding, assisting over 300 companies, and helping create more than 3,000 jobs.

HTDC serves technology startups, manufacturers, and innovation-driven businesses in Hawaii. Its programs target sectors including aerospace, ocean technologies, clean energy, and general manufacturing. The agency works with small and medium-sized manufacturers seeking productivity improvements, tech entrepreneurs needing incubation and capital, and energy researchers focused on hydrogen technology.

HTDC was created to address the need for economic diversification in Hawaii by developing a sustainable technology and innovation ecosystem that fosters collaboration, entrepreneurship, and technological advancement, aiming to create quality, high-paying jobs for residents.

The farm grows legumes, ancient grains, berries, vegetables, and flowers, and maintains bees for raw honey. It runs a stone mill on site to produce flour from its own grains. A farm shop and mill house are part of the facility, though the shop was closed for restructuring as of the latest update. Products are sold directly to consumers at the Gallatin Valley Farmers Market in Bozeman on Saturdays from June through September, and at the Bozeman Winter Market on Saturdays from October through May. The farm does not list wholesale or industrial customers in its public materials.

The company states its mission is to heal the biology of the farm—linking soil health, plant health, and human health—and to share the resulting bounty. Regenerative practices are presented as the core differentiator, with the goal of increasing the nutritional quality of the food grown.

about:
Founded in 1969 in Houston, Texas, Houston Transformer Company, LTD. has operated as a privately held manufacturer of custom magnetic devices. The company began with a focus on wound magnetics for demanding applications and has remained headquartered in its original city.

The company designs and builds custom transformers, inductors, chokes, reactors, and coils ranging from sub-miniature surface-mount devices to three-phase units weighing over 1,500 pounds. Its 33,000-square-foot climate-controlled facility houses an on-site machine shop and sheet-metal department that produce metal bobbins, cases, NEMA-rated enclosures, and custom core configurations. The shop maintains an inventory of roughly 25,000 pounds of high-grade silicon steel to shorten cycle times, and the engineering team brings more than 75 years of combined design experience. Headcount falls in the 51-to-200 range.

Houston Transformer serves original equipment manufacturers and single-piece buyers across energy exploration, drilling operations, medical and biomedical equipment, military and aerospace programs, audio and lighting systems, data processing, industrial process control, and communications. Products have been used in downhole tools operating above 250 °C, in medical instruments, and in high-reliability defense systems.

The company emphasizes a 'can-do' philosophy, fast prototyping, and adherence to UL and other industry standards. Its quality policy targets continuous improvement through a monitored quality management system, while its safety policy prioritizes an injury-free workplace. These commitments, along with in-house fabrication of cores and enclosures, are cited as key differentiators.

name: IHI Connectors - Manufacturing Facility
old_description: High Quality, USA made electrical lugs sold at factory direct prices
about:
IHI Connectors, the trade name of International Hydraulics Inc., operates its main office, assembly, and warehouse at 7700 St. Clair Avenue in Mentor, Ohio. The company produces high-tensile tin-plated aluminum electrical lugs and mechanical screw-type connectors for stranded and solid aluminum and copper wire.

Its product line includes single-, double-, triple-, and multi-wire lugs, splicer reducers, through-hole and surface-mount PCB terminal lugs rated from 20 to 300 amps, and custom OEM designs. The facility supports blanket orders with weekly, monthly, or quarterly releases and stocks standard parts in quantities from single pieces to full boxes. Representative PCB lugs include the B6B-PCB (65 A, 6–14 AWG), B4B-PCB-B (95 A, 4–14 AWG, all-copper body), and B2/0-PCB (175 A, 2/0–8 AWG). STEP files are available for all catalog items.

The company serves the smart-energy and renewable-energy sectors, supplying components for EV chargers, inverter battery-backup systems, server-farm power supplies, solar installations, industrial furnaces, and motion-control servo power supplies. Customers range from volume buyers ordering direct through the LugsDirect.com channel to OEMs requiring custom connectors quoted to print.

IHI Connectors emphasizes U.S. manufacturing and factory-direct pricing. Its patented Tork Krimp® lugs accept ferrules without pre-crimping, eliminating special tools and labor. The firm also offers the broadest range of high-current PCB terminal lugs on the market and holds UL and CSA approvals for fine-stranded wire classes G, H, I, DLO, K, MTW, welding, and battery cable up to 444 kcmil. A CAGE code (7RPR4) enables government contracting.

Impact Imports was founded in 2001 in Boise, Idaho, as a source for distinctive artifacts imported from Indonesia. The company began with a focus on supplying refined materials—stone vessel sinks, live‑edge wood slabs, and reclaimed teak—to designers and property owners seeking natural, organic elements for residential and commercial spaces.

Today the operation runs a warehouse showroom in Boise where customers can view inventory Thursday through Saturday or by appointment. The product range spans petrified‑wood and river‑rock vessel sinks, onyx and marble pedestal sinks, boulder bathtubs, natural‑stone fire pits, and a line of USA‑made rectangular gas fire tables branded IMPACT Fire Tables. The team also assists clients with custom furniture projects, offering sawing and flattening services for jumbo wood slabs and supplying finished dining tables, coffee tables, and accent pieces crafted from sustainably harvested, kiln‑dried lumber.

The primary customers are residential homeowners, hospitality operators such as lodges, eateries, and cafes, and commercial office developers. Interior designers and architects also source materials for projects that call for unique stone and wood features.

Impact Imports differentiates itself through its long‑standing Indonesian supply relationships, its emphasis on sustainably harvested and kiln‑dried wood, hand‑crafted stone fire pits, and the domestic manufacture of its IMPACT Fire Tables using CorTen steel and powder‑coated aluminum components.

about:
ITW Food Equipment Group is headquartered in Troy, Ohio, and traces its roots to 1830 when the Bonnet brand began designing, manufacturing, and installing professional kitchen equipment in Europe. The group operates as a division of Illinois Tool Works (ITW), bringing together a family of premium brands that have served foodservice and food retail professionals for over a century.

The company designs and manufactures a broad range of commercial cooking, refrigeration, warewashing, and bakery equipment under brands including Hobart, Traulsen, Baxter, Vulcan, Wolf, Stero, Foster, and Bonnet. Its innovation pipeline has produced nearly 600 ENERGY STAR® certified products, driven by more than 1,000 staff members who hold at least one invention and a 70% patent commercialization rate reported in 2013. A service network of nearly 200 offices and 1,500 factory-trained technicians covers 95% of customers within 50 miles, complemented by the SmartConnect365 remote-monitoring platform.

ITW Food Equipment serves the foodservice, food retail, bakery, and institutional catering sectors, including restaurants, hotels, schools, and healthcare facilities. Wholesale and production bakery suppliers also rely on its equipment for high-volume operations.

The group emphasizes customer-driven innovation and sustainable leadership, earning the U.S. EPA’s ENERGY STAR Partner of the Year award every year since 2008 and the Sustained Excellence Award in 2024. Brands such as Foster have achieved the Carbon Trust Standard for carbon reduction, while technologies like Hobart’s Advansys energy recovery system cut energy costs by up to 50% and water use by 90% in dishwashing.

International Wire, headquartered in Camden, New York, traces its origins to 1885. The company has grown through strategic acquisitions to become the largest non-vertically integrated manufacturer of copper and copper-alloy wire products in the United States.

The company produces copper single-end wire (44 AWG to 2 AWG), stranded wire, braided wire, flat wire, and copper wire on bobbins. Specific applications include robotics, factory automation, solar farms, wind turbines, nuclear energy, in-flight entertainment and cabin management wiring, airframe conductors, 5G network infrastructure, electric vehicle systems, medical devices, and building wiring and grounding.

International Wire states its mission is to provide quality, value-oriented, copper-based products and services that exceed customer expectations, guided by core values of safety, people, customers, products and services, integrity, and continuous improvement. The firm differentiates itself through a streamlined, collaborative process, a broad material palette sourced within a 100-mile radius, and a commitment to sustainability that diverts urban lumber from landfills. It imposes no minimum or maximum order quantities and emphasizes shorter lead times through in-house capabilities.

Idaho Supreme Potatoes operates from Firth, Idaho, where it began as a fresh potato packing operation in 1967. The facility expanded into potato dehydration in 1969 and grew into one of North America's dehydration plants. In 2018, Idaho Pacific Holdings acquired the company and continues its tradition of supplying dehydrated potato products worldwide.

The plant produces dehydrated potato flakes, flour, slices, dices, and shreds or hash browns, with ingredient specifications ranging from whole flake to finely milled flours, full cook to low leach, and additive-free clean label options. Foodservice lines include complete mashed potato mixes (blended or agglomerated), scalloped and au gratin casseroles, and seasoned or unseasoned hash browns. An in-house R&D team develops custom formulations, while packaging runs cover poly pouches, gabled cartons, #10 tins, kraft bags, polyethylene bulk sacks, and bulk rail or truck shipments. Private labeling is available for most foodservice and retail items.

Customers span foodservice distributors, retail brands, and industrial ingredient users across North America. The company sources Russet varieties such as Burbank, Norkotah, and Ranger from Idaho's Snake River Plain, leveraging the region's soil, water, and climate for consistent year-round supply.

Idaho Supreme Potatoes emphasizes its diverse production capabilities and certifications—GFSI, Orthodox Union kosher, and IFANCA halal—as the foundation for meeting varied technical and regulatory requirements.

Imondi Foods serves independent bakeries, commercial bakeries, and food manufacturers throughout the Northeast. Its customer base includes operations that rely on consistent, daily delivery of perishable and dry ingredients, with the company's purchasing power enabling wholesale pricing across a broad product catalog.

The business was built on dependable service, quality products, and lasting customer relationships — principles established at its founding and reinforced by certifications and a family-led management team that emphasizes personal connection over transactional volume.

about:
Indiana Rubber & Plastic, LLC was founded in 1936 in Indianapolis, Indiana, and has operated continuously for three generations. The company began as a specialist in custom molded plastics and rubber and has expanded its capabilities while remaining focused on its core expertise.

The company provides turnkey service from prototyping through high-volume production. Its processes include rubber molding (compression, transfer, injection, and LSR/LIM), plastic injection molding, extrusion of both plastics and rubber, die cutting, lathe-cut rubber, machined plastics, and bonded rubber-to-metal components. Prototyping uses 3D printing, SLA, rapid molding, and silicone molds. Production volumes span prototype runs of 1–50 pieces, short runs of 1–5,000 pieces, medium runs of 5,000–25,000 pieces, and high-volume orders exceeding 25,000 pieces. The facility operates high-tonnage presses with large platens for oversized parts and maintains on-site tooling to match mold size to demand.

Indiana Rubber & Plastic serves customers requiring custom molded rubber and plastic components, including those needing food-grade and military-specification materials. Its product portfolio includes grommets, gaskets, seals, bumpers, diaphragms, bushings, extrusions, mounts, formed hoses, boots, and washers or spacers.

The company differentiates itself through competitive pricing driven by innovation, an in-house technical team of designers, CAD drafters, chemists, and laboratory resources, plus access to custom compounders. It emphasizes a "plastics and rubber" breadth—adding urethane, silicone, and thermoplastic elastomers—and a commitment to staying within its three generations of core knowledge. Transparent communication throughout the supply cycle and proprietary Amazing Tool$aver® low-cost tooling methods further define its approach.

about:
Industrial Semiconductor, Inc. was founded in 1991 by Fred Marquardt in Granville, Illinois. Marquardt’s career began in a radio and TV repair shop before he joined the United States Air Force, where he worked on vacuum tube and solid-state electronics. He later became part of the SCR development team at National Electronics, contributing to manufacturing innovations and serving on the JEDEC Industry Standards Committee. The business incorporated in 2004, and in 2015 ownership transferred to Steven Malavolti, a 20-year U.S. Navy veteran and former chief petty officer, who had joined the company in 2007 and became general manager in 2010.

The company operates as a mainline stocking distributor of high-power semiconductors, including SCRs, diodes, bridge modules, thyristor modules, diode modules, and GTOs from manufacturers such as Dynex, Times Electric, RIRI Power Electronics, GE, Westinghouse, Infineon, Powerex, Mitsubishi, Westcode, and IXYS. In addition to distribution, Industrial Semiconductor provides heatsink extrusion and assembles air-cooled thyristor, diode-heatsink, and SCR-heatsink assemblies. The Granville facility maintains an extensive inventory with same-day shipping and no minimum order requirement.

Customers span the power electronics, automotive racing, and renewable energy sectors. Early projects included solid-state timing systems for SCCA and NASCAR racing, as well as portable timing for Ford Motor Company’s road racing team. More recently, the company serves the wind turbine energy market and broader industrial power applications, working directly with engineers and OEMs who require technical problem-solving rather than transactional sales.

Industrial Semiconductor distinguishes itself by avoiding e-commerce automation in favor of direct voice and email contact, staffing technical problem solvers who know the product line. The company sells only new, factory-tested components to original OEM specifications, aiming to build a long-term team that can meet evolving power industry needs.

Integra serves surgeons, hospitals, and healthcare systems worldwide, with a focus on neurosurgery, plastic and reconstructive surgery, wound care, and ENT specialties. The company positions its manufacturing operations as purpose-driven, emphasizing evidence-based regenerative technologies and long-standing innovation such as the 20-year history of CUSA® technology. Its stated mission centers on restoring lives through everyday impact, combining global leadership in neurosurgery with immersive surgical education.

about:
Intelligent Manufacturing Solutions (IMS) was founded in 2005 in Londonderry, New Hampshire. The company was purpose-built to address a service gap for high-quality, rapid prototype and small-lot printed circuit board assembly. The founders, whose names are not publicly disclosed, recognized the struggles businesses faced in receiving responsive customer service for prototype and low-volume PCBA needs. In December 2024, IMS was acquired by Perimeter Solutions (NYSE: PRM), which aims to broaden its portfolio and add a new business model for acquiring and supporting OEM legacy product lines.

IMS provides full life-cycle electronics assembly services, including rapid prototype assembly, high-mix flexible manufacturing, design-for-manufacturing (DFM) analysis, end-of-life support, box build, short-notice production, and build-to-order manufacturing. The New England facility houses multiple SMT pick-and-place lines (Mycronic MY300, M100, MY9E), three Heller 1808 MkIII reflow ovens, solder paste inspection and deposition equipment (Mycronic Primo 3D SPI, MY600, MY500, SpeedPrint SP710, MPM Accuflex), X-ray and AOI inspection (UniComp AX8200, Mirtec MV6 Omni), rework stations (VJ Electronics Summit), selective soldering (Nordson Novo 103, Ace 102, Hollis TDL wave), and aqueous cleaning systems. The company emphasizes quick turnaround, stating it can start production the day an order is received and ship assemblies within hours. No specific headcount or facility square footage is disclosed.

IMS serves aerospace and defense, medical and instrumentation, communications, consumer electronics/IoT, automotive, and industrial sectors. Customer testimonials cite an automotive technology company, a consumer robotics company, and an IoT solutions provider. The company supports OEMs needing rapid prototyping, low-volume production, and end-of-life product sustainment.

IMS was started to fill a market gap for responsive, high-quality prototype and low-volume PCBA services. The company differentiates itself through a culture of responsiveness, on-time delivery, and a direct order fulfillment model that helps customers grow. Its acquisition by Perimeter Solutions adds a model for acquiring and licensing OEM legacy product lines to sustain them through their remaining lifecycle.

about:
Inter-Coastal Electronics (ICE) operates from Mesa, Arizona, and serves as the current Tactical Engagement Simulation System (TESS) Program of Record holder for U.S. Army aviation. The company provides embedded training solutions built on three decades of experience in live, virtual, and constructive training environments.

ICE designs, develops, manufactures, tests, delivers, and supports live training systems that increase warfighter effectiveness and survivability. Its product portfolio includes TESS production kits with ground support equipment, the TOW-ITAS Laser Integrated Field Training System (LIFTS), the Training ASE Stimulation Suite (TASS), and the Army TADSS Maintenance Program (ATMP). The company handles engineering, production planning, depot repair, supply chain management, and systems integration for ruggedized electronics and embedded systems.

ICE supports U.S. Army aviation platforms at Combat Training Centers including the National Training Center (NTC), Joint Readiness Training Center (JRTC), and Joint Multinational Readiness Center (JMRC). International customers include the Netherlands, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, Qatar, and Morocco, with programs covering AH-64E Apache, UH-60M Black Hawk, CH-47F Chinook, and TOW missile systems.

The company emphasizes a low-risk, cost-effective approach that provides immediate interoperability with existing Army ranges and a Modular Open Systems Architecture (MOSA) to reduce lifecycle costs. Leadership includes veterans with extensive Army aviation and acquisition experience, guiding a strategy focused on readiness, proficiency, and affordability.

old_description: We offer a complete line of agricultural fencing products that meet or exceed industry standards. By devising new industry products and improving the functionality of existing products, Oklahoma and Iowa Steel & Wire Companies make the products you can depend on. about:
Iowa Steel & Wire Co operates in Centerville, Iowa, as part of the OKBRAND family of companies founded in 1979 by B. L. Moore and his brother-in-law Robert Lockridge in Madill, Oklahoma. The Moore family reopened the Iowa facility in 1989 to focus on industrial wire products, and the family continues to own and direct daily operations today.

The company produces a complete line of agricultural fencing — including livestock panels, barbed wire, field fence, and horse-safe Max-Tight and Max-Loc systems — as well as industrial wire products such as welded wire fabric, commodity mesh, mine mesh, box culverts, pipe fabric, and structural reinforcement. Production is vertically integrated: an electric arc furnace melts 100% recycled scrap into billets, a rolling mill forms wire rod, and multiple EVG and Schlatter welders with high-speed straight-and-cut lines handle fabrication.

Customers span agriculture, construction, mining, and infrastructure markets. Fencing distributors and contractors specify OKBRAND panels and horse fence; mines and precast concrete suppliers use the company’s welded mesh and culvert reinforcement; structural fabricators source wire for reinforcement.

The Moore family’s philosophy emphasizes continuous improvement, employee safety, and competitive pricing. Vertical integration and domestic melting allow the company to control quality and lead times, while a product warranty backs every shipment.

The business was started to meet local demand for a full-service fabrication shop that could handle both one-off custom jobs and ongoing repair work.

name: Iron Work Studio
old_description: Manufacturing high quality, custom iron products for your home since 1997.
about:
Iron Work Studio operates from Owings, Maryland, where it has been based for over two decades. The company was founded in 1997 by Rob Link, a third‑generation welder who started with a 200‑square‑foot warehouse in nearby Severn before moving the shop closer to home. Link, who holds a technical degree in electronic engineering and a background in the steamfitters’ union, built the business from the ground up, purchasing equipment and hiring a full‑time crew as demand grew.

The studio produces custom ironwork for residential clients, ranging from fine‑art pieces such as chandeliers, tables, and railings to large‑scale architectural installations. Core processes include welding, fabricating, CNC plasma cutting, and computer‑aided design using AutoCAD. A four‑person team handles projects from initial drawings through final assembly, working with iron, steel, and sheet metal in a shop equipped with a CNC plasma cutting machine.

Primary customers are homeowners, interior designers, and architects seeking bespoke metal elements for homes. The company’s portfolio highlights decorative and structural items for private residences, with an emphasis on artistic metalwork that blends function and aesthetics.

Link’s family welding heritage and hands‑on management style are cited as the foundation of the studio’s approach. The firm stresses precision, attention to detail, and the ability to take a project from concept to completion without outsourcing.

name: Ironwood Mills
old_description: We’re looking for someone with a genuine interest and passion for custom fabrication and
about:
Ironwood Mills operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where founder Scott Mills established the company in 2016. After more than two decades as an independent contractor, Mills turned a lifelong fascination with wood—sparked by a tool kit at age six—into a business that rescues discarded trees from the Phoenix metro area and transforms them into custom furniture and live‑edge slabs. The “urban lumber” model began with Mills personally hunting for unique logs in the desert, a practice that now feeds a small team of woodworkers.

The shop at 8342 N. 7th Street houses a Lucas Mill 10‑30 (cuts logs up to 5′ diameter, 21′ long), a hydraulic Wood‑Mizer bandsaw, a Wood Wizz surfacing machine (up to 7 × 17 feet), and an iDRY vacuum kiln. Services include custom furniture fabrication, milling ($150/hour, one‑hour minimum), machine surfacing ($150/hour), and kiln drying ($2/board foot, 1,000‑board‑foot minimum). The team—Mills, Kit Vander Jagt (20 years’ experience), and Michael Toret (10+ years, including theatrical scenery and welding)—produces one‑off pieces and small batches.

Primary customers are interior designers, architects, professional woodworkers, and homeowners. Designers source slabs and collaborate on custom tables and specialty items; woodworkers bring material for surfacing and kiln drying; homeowners commission finished furniture. The company also hosts team‑building workshops.

Ironwood Mills differentiates itself through its urban‑lumber supply chain—turning neighborhood trees that would otherwise be chipped into furniture‑grade material—and through vacuum‑kiln drying that eliminates raised grain and reduces drying time. Mills describes the mission as a privilege: “to take a forgotten & unwanted tree and bring it back to life.”
